paragraphs: The modern theory of edit distance was built through a sequence of landmark papers rather than a single algorithmic invention. Vladimir Levenshtein's 1965 Russian paper, published in English translation in 1966, established the insertion-deletion-substitution sequence geometry that now bears his name; Wagner and Fischer later gave the canonical dynamic-programming treatment of string-to-string correction; Masek and Paterson demonstrated that exact computation could beat straightforward quadratic tabulation under suitable assumptions; Ukkonen and Landau-Vishkin developed distance-sensitive and bounded approximate-matching methods; Myers introduced highly practical bit-vector dynamic programming; Navarro synthesized the mature approximate-string-matching literature; Schulz and Mihov developed efficient Levenshtein automata; and Backurs and Indyk connected the persistent near-quadratic complexity of exact edit distance to modern conditional lower-bound theory. This section examines those original publications as scholarly works—their definitions, algorithms, proofs, assumptions, complexity claims, historical context, and what later literature did or did not derive from them.

01 Backurs–Indyk 2015: SETH Hardness of Edit Distance, Orthogonal Vectors, and the Strongly Subquadratic Barrier A rigorous analysis of Backurs–Indyk 2015: SETH, Orthogonal Vectors, edit-distance gadgets, the O(n²−δ) barrier, later refinements, and limitations. Article · 44 min read

02 Schulz–Mihov 2002: Levenshtein Automata, Linear-Time Construction, and Fast Dictionary Correction Deep analysis of Schulz–Mihov 2002: deterministic Levenshtein automata, characteristic vectors, parametric transitions, O(|W|) construction, and fast dictionary correction. Article · 59 min read

03 Navarro 2001: A Guided Tour to Approximate String Matching, Algorithms, Filters, Automata, and Bit Parallelism A rigorous analysis of Navarro’s 2001 survey: edit-distance search, dynamic programming, automata, bit parallelism, filtering, experiments, and open problems. Article · 48 min read

04 Myers 1999: Bit-Vector Edit Distance, Relocatable Dynamic Programming, and Approximate String Matching A rigorous analysis of Myers's 1999 bit-vector algorithm, covering relocatable DP, Pv/Mv masks, carry propagation, O(n⌈m/w⌉) time, long-pattern blocks, and limitations. Article · 51 min read

05 Landau–Vishkin 1988: Fast String Matching with k Differences, Approximate Pattern Matching, and Error-Bounded Search A rigorous analysis of Landau and Vishkin's 1988 paper on approximate pattern matching with k differences, covering edit operations, DP diagonals, error frontiers, preprocessing, O(nk²) search, space bounds, and its later O(nk) lineage. Article · 58 min read

06 Ukkonen 1985: Algorithms for Approximate String Matching, Banded DP, and Distance-Sensitive Edit Distance A rigorous analysis of Ukkonen's 1985 paper on threshold bands, O(s·min(m,n)) edit distance, unit-cost frontiers, LCS, and transpositions. Article · 59 min read

07 Masek–Paterson 1980: Four Russians Edit Distance, Block Precomputation, and the O(n²/log n) Algorithm A rigorous analysis of Masek and Paterson's 1980 edit-distance paper, covering Four Russians blocking, step vectors, discrete edit costs, preprocessing, O(n²/log n) time, edit-path recovery, LCS, and limitations. Article · 49 min read

08 Wagner–Fischer 1974: The String-to-String Correction Problem, Dynamic Programming, and Edit Distance A rigorous analysis of Wagner and Fischer's 1974 paper, covering weighted edit distance, traces, the dynamic-programming recurrence, correctness proofs, traceback, O(mn) complexity, and longest common subsequences. Article · 44 min read

09 Levenshtein 1965/1966 Paper: Binary Codes, Edit Distance, and Deletion-Correcting Codes A rigorous analysis of Levenshtein's 1965/1966 foundational paper, covering deletion-insertion metrics, VT codes, asymptotic bounds, reversals, decoding, and synchronization. Article · 36 min read
